text:
alex: Ran an nsys capture on a 4-GPU pod — timeline looks like memcpy blocks then big kernel bursts. putting the trace here: https://perf.redwood/internal/2109876543 (nsys import)
maria: saw that. do you have the kernel names?
alex: key ones: prefetch_kv_cache, kv_insert_kernel, attention_fwd, copy_engine_memcpy. interestingly the memcpy (host->device) sits on a separate stream but still serializes with kernels.
sam: can you paste the nsys command you used? want to re-run with thread-level CPU sampling.
alex: sure:```nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --output=kv-prefetch-probe ./run_infer.sh --model tiny --batch 8``` also used `nsys stats` after to dump timeline.
kari: my hot take: looks like host-side memcpy is using pageable memory so copy engine stalls and CPU threads wake/handle the copy, causing kernel queues to wait on new CTAs. CPU preemption gaps line up with the big memcpy boxes.
maria: +1. pageable H2D often forces synchronous behaviour when the driver needs to pin pages at copy time.
sam: i re-ran with `cudaMemcpyAsync` + `cudaHostAlloc(..., cudaHostAllocMapped | cudaHostAllocWriteCombined)` and captured: memcpy is smaller and overlaps better, but still occasional 2-3ms gaps where nothing's running on GPU.
perf-bot: [capture analysis] top CPU waiters: prefetch-thread-1, prefetch-thread-2; top kernels by time: attention_fwd (42%), prefetch_kv_cache (18%), kv_insert_kernel (12%).
kari: can we try bumping the affinity/priority of prefetch threads? e.g. `chrt -f 1 <pid>` or `taskset -c 2` to pin to isolated cpu? my suspicion: linux scheduler preempts the thread that kickstarts the copy.
maria: also try using pinned host buffers for the entire batch path + `cudaMemcpyAsync` on a separate non-default stream for copies. that should let copy engine truly overlap.
alex: timeline excerpt (nsys waterfall):```[GPU0] ----copy----||--attention_fwd--||--prefetch--||--attention_fwd--
[GPU1] ----copy----||--stall---------||--attention_fwd--
CPU:  wake(prethred) ... preempt ... wake(prethread)``` you can see copy boxes cause 5-7ms stall windows on other streams.
sam: noted another pattern: kv_insert_kernel uses a lot of device-to-device memcpy inside kernel (memcpy.smem). could be blocking because of shared memory bank conflicts, not just hostcopy. need nvprof-ish counters for shared mem throughput.
kari: agree. add an nvtx push at kv_insert start/end and capture `nvprof --analysis-metrics` or CUPTI counters to see shared mem/utilization.
maria: small experiment idea: change batcher to pre-warm pinned buffers and pre-issue host->device copies as soon as prompt decoding starts (prefix caching). amortize hostcopy latency across idle periods.
alex: good plan. i'll run two captures tomorrow: (A) pinned buffers + cudaMemcpyAsync; (B) same but set prefetch threads SCHED_FIFO. will attach both traces.
sam: i'll instrument kv_insert with bank-stress test to see if shared mem is the culprit.
kari: if SCHED_FIFO fixes the gaps that's a pretty strong signal it's CPU preemption. but note risks — SCHED_FIFO can starve other processes. do it on staging only.
maria: also add a metric to track copy-engine occupancy (from nsys) and host-page-fault counts during capture.
alex: ok owners: alex = run captures A/B, sam = kv_insert microbench, kari = priority experiments, maria = modify batcher to pre-warm pinned buffers. i'll post traces in this thread. thanks :thumbsup:
